member.name: T:PSDataRepository.Commands.Common.CryptoHelper
member.summary:
Provides AES-256 encryption and decryption with Argon2id (current) or PBKDF2 (legacy) key derivation. Shared by Compress-PSDataRepositoryItem and Expand-PSDataRepositoryItem cmdlets.
V5 format (AES-GCM, Argon2id m=19456 t=2 p=1, default): [PSDR-ENC-V5 11B][Salt 32B][Nonce 12B][Tag 16B][Ciphertext]
V4 format (AES-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA512, 210k iterations, legacy read): [PSDR-ENC-V4 11B][Salt 32B][Nonce 12B][Tag 16B][Ciphertext]

V2 format (AES-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256, 100k iterations, legacy read): [PSDR-ENC-V2 11B][Salt 32B][Nonce 12B][Tag 16B][Ciphertext]
V1 format (AES-CBC, legacy read-only): [PSDR-ENC-V1 11B][Salt 32B][IV 16B][Ciphertext]

member.name: T:PSDataRepository.Commands.Common.ExtensionInstallHelper
member.summary:
Layout rules shared by the extension install/uninstall cmdlets.
The module's on-disk shape is dictated by the loader: it computes the module directory from the location of PSDataRepository.Core.dll — which lives in {ModuleRoot}/bin/{TFM}/ — then scans {ModuleRoot}/bin/{TFM}/{Subfolder}/ for plugins and resolves their dependencies from {ModuleRoot}/bin/{TFM}/. Anything placed elsewhere is simply never discovered, so every path decision here mirrors that layout rather than inventing one.

summary.para: Lists the extensions the module discovered at import time, including the ones it refused to load and why.

Extensions are plugin assemblies dropped into the module's Auth\, Providers\ and Formatters\ folders. Loading one can fail for reasons that are invisible from the outside — the assembly is unsigned, its public key token is not trusted, or it was built against an incompatible contract version — and the only symptom is a provider or formatter that does not exist.

This cmdlet reports every candidate assembly the loader saw, whether it loaded, and the reason for each rejection. The scan happens once when the module is imported, so results reflect that scan; restart PowerShell after adding or replacing an extension.

example.para: Lists every discovered extension with its status and contract version.
Shows only the extensions that were refused, with the full explanation.
Limits the report to formatter extensions.

member.summary: Return only extensions the loader refused to load.

member.summary: Limit the report to one plugin subfolder.

member.name: P:PSDataRepository.Commands.GetPSDataRepositoryExtensionCommand.VersionSkew
member.summary:
Compare each extension's referenced assembly versions against what is actually present in the module folder, and report the differences.
An extension binds at runtime to whatever version sits in the module root, not the one it was compiled against. A mismatch is invisible until the moment a missing member is touched, which is usually long after the install that caused it — most often a module upgrade or another extension replacing a shared library.

member.name: P:PSDataRepository.Commands.GetPSDataRepositoryExtensionCommand.MissingAfterUpgrade
member.summary:
Also report extensions that an earlier installed version of the module had, but this one does not.
Every module version is installed into its own folder, so upgrading the module produces an empty one: every extension silently disappears and has to be reinstalled. Nothing announces that — the module works, the in-box providers and formatters are all there, and only the third-party ones are gone. This compares the dependency manifest left behind in the previous version's folder against what is installed here.

member.name: P:PSDataRepository.Commands.GetPSDataRepositoryExtensionCommand.ModuleRoot
member.summary: Which module installation to compare for . Defaults to the running module. Does not affect the rest of the report, which always reflects the scan performed by the running module at import time.

member.name: M:PSDataRepository.Commands.GetPSDataRepositoryExtensionCommand.GetVersionSkew(System.String)
member.summary:
Lists assemblies the extension was compiled against whose version differs from the one actually sitting in the module folder it will bind to.
Only assemblies present in the module root are compared. A referenced assembly that is absent there is either part of the shared framework or genuinely missing, and the loader reports the latter as a load failure already.

summary.para: Installs a PSDataRepository extension into the installed module from a local artifact or a registered NuGet repository.

Places an extension's assemblies into the module's bin\{TFM}\{Subfolder}\ layout — the only location the loader scans — and copies its dependencies alongside the host assemblies where the plugin load context can resolve them.

Before anything is written, every candidate assembly is inspected the same way the loader inspects it: it must be strong-named, and its declared contract version must be one this module can satisfy. Catching an incompatible extension here turns what would otherwise be a silently missing provider after the next restart into an error at install time.

Trust is deliberately NOT granted automatically. An extension signed with a key the module does not already trust is installed but will not load until its public key token is added to extensions.trust.json; pass -Trust to do that as part of the install, which is an explicit decision to let that publisher's code run.

example.para: Installs from the artifact produced by publish-extension.ps1. No .NET SDK required.
Installs a single assembly and trusts its signing key.
Shows what would be installed from a registered PSResource repository.

summary.para: Removes an installed PSDataRepository extension from the module.
Deletes the extension assembly from every bin\{TFM}\{Subfolder}\ folder it is found in, together with the dependencies it introduced.

Dependency cleanup is driven by the manifest Install-PSDataRepositoryExtension wrote (extensions.deps.json). A file is removed only when this extension brought it into a module that did not have it, and no other installed extension lists it. Anything that pre-existed belongs to the module itself, and anything another extension still needs stays — the module root is shared, so deleting the wrong file there breaks something else. An extension installed before that manifest existed has nothing recorded, so only its own assembly is removed.
Trust is not revoked unless -RemoveTrust is given, and revoking a token affects every extension signed with that key, not just this one.

Clears out extensions the loader refused to load.
